arXiv:2609.26544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating strongly correlated fermions remains a long-standing challenge due to the exponential complexity of the Hilbert space and the intricate sign structure of many-body wavefunctions. item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hassan Ugail, Newton Howard
Every noise channel acting on a quantum neural network leaves a structural signature in the way it decays the coherences of the circuit, and this paper shows that the signature can be read before any training takes place. For the noise families that dominate practical device models, the decay rates within a charge sector of an equivariant network assemble into a weighted graph with closed-form edge weights, and the trainability behaviour of the circuit is organised by this coherence-rate graph. We prove a sufficient protection theorem on the graph, certified by a purely combinatorial construction from the circuit connectivity, we validate a predictor of the depth at which correlated noise degrades each trainable parameter, and we derive exact product laws for the measured degradation.
